id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

xp.description: Total XP points of the user.

badges.description: Array of badges earned by the user.

streak.description: Current learning streak of the user.

Course.description: Represents a coding course available on the platform.

language.description: Programming language taught in the course (e.g., Python, Java).

levelIds.description: References to Level entities included in the course. (Relationship: Course 1:N Level)

Level.title: Level
Level.description: Represents a level within a coding course.

levelNumber.description: The number of the level within the course.

gameIds.description: References to Game entities included in the level. (Relationship: Level 1:N Game)

Game.title: Game
Game.description: Represents a game within a level.

type.description: Type of game (e.g., MCQ, fill-in-the-blank, drag-and-drop).

content.description: The actual data/content of the game, likely serialized as JSON.

Certificate.title: Certificate
Certificate.description: Represents a certificate earned by a user upon completing a course.

completionDate.description: Date when the course was completed.

certificateURL.description: URL where the certificate can be downloaded.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the 'Code Conqueror' application, focusing on user authentication, personalized learning experiences, gamified coding modules, and certificate generation. The structure emphasizes Authorization Independence and supports QAPs by segregating data based on ownership and access needs. User data and profile information are separated into distinct collections, enabling efficient querying and management. Course content and progress are structured to facilitate a gamified learning experience. Ownership is explicit via path-based structures. The following design decisions were made:

*   **Authorization Independence:** User-owned data (profiles, progress) are stored under `/users/{userId}` paths. This ensures that access control can be enforced without needing to read parent documents.  Since the application doesn't require collaborative data structures, no membership maps or denormalization of authorization data is needed.
*   **Structural Segregation:** User profiles are stored under `/users/{userId}/profiles/{profileId}`, allowing for distinct security rules compared to course or game data. Course and level content is stored in separate top-level collections. This enables efficient querying and management of each type of data. Certificates are stored under `/users/{userId}/certificates/{certificateId}`.
*   **Access Modeling:** Path-based ownership is enforced for user-related data. Courses, levels, and games are globally accessible, but write access is restricted to admin roles (if implemented).
*   **Data Clarity and Predictability:**  Entity names are used as collection names, with clear relationships between documents. Explicit state modeling (e.g., a `status` field for courses) is not applicable in this design, but could be added in the future for managing course publication status or similar features. Each User 1:1 UserProfile will make rules clear and concise.
